newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss stocks end down, but above early lows.
newsitem.headline: Swiss stocks end down, but above early lows.

text.p: Swiss shares ended lower, but above early losses of some three percent, as last week's consolidation continued, dealers said.
Bargain hunting helped the shares recover after initial losses, dealers said.
"It was a far cry from 1987," alluding to 1987's "Black Monday" crash.
One dealer said insecurity may cease after Tuesday and Wednesday's meeting by the U.S. Federal Reserve and Thursday's German Bundesbank meeting.
In late trade, the firming tendency on Wall Street was another positive factor.
While some dealers thought the correction may be over, others said the prices may continue to fall.
The blue-chip SMI was down 92.9 points or 1.69 percent at 5,405.6. The day's low was at 5,278.3 points which was below the critical level of 5,300 points.
All-share Swiss Performance Index (SPI) gave up 55.11 points, or 1.55 percent, to 3,492.01.
Bourse volume reached an above-average 3.74 billion Swiss francs.
Dealers said derivatives-related transactions and profit taking put the market under pressure, especially in early trade.
Most blue chips were lower. Novartis registered shares were down 42 francs to 2,135, while Roche was down 10 francs to 13,315.
Dollar-sensitive Surveillance and insurer Baloise were among the day's winners, advancing 20 francs to 3,015 and 70 francs to 3,940, respectively.
Baloise has been sought recently after merger plans of bank group Credit Suisse Group and insurer Winterthur led to renewed speculations about Baloise being another possible takeover object.
